text:
Here are the strongest 3-in-1 Qi2 stands from the reviews I found. Prices are as of each review and change often.

**Best overall: Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand (~$80–98)**
WIRED's top pick. It charges an iPhone at up to 15W, handles the Apple Watch, and has a spot for AirPods. It's a good value, though it's slower than the 25W models. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))

**Fastest for a desk: Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable Qi2 25W (~$129.99)**
Macworld calls it the tallest and most adjustable foldable 3-in-1 it has tested. It delivers 25W to a supported iPhone, has a fast Apple Watch module, and includes a 45W adapter and UK/EU plugs. It weighs about 399g, so it's less portable. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html))

**Best for nightstand use: Nimble Podium 3-in-1 (~$130)**
The phone and watch pads can lie flat so the screens stay out of sight, and they can pop up for StandBy mode. It supports Qi2 25W for iPhone. The Apple Watch charges slowly, so it's best overnight. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))

**Best fast travel option: ESR CryoBoost Qi2 25W 3-in-1 (~$100)**
It folds, supports 25W for compatible iPhones, and has a fan with an off switch for quiet nights. The plastic build feels less premium, and the 25W speed mostly matters if you're not charging overnight. ([WIRED travel guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/))

**Budget pick: ESR Qi2 3-in-1 (~$40–80)**
It charges the iPhone at 15W. The Apple Watch charger is a separate unit that plugs into the back, so the setup is less integrated. Its 1-year warranty is shorter than the others'. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))

**My suggestion:** For a nightstand, go with the Nimble Podium if you have a 16 or 17 series iPhone. For a desk, choose the Satechi. If you want the best value, the Belkin is the strongest 15W option.

I couldn't find direct merchant product links in these results, so search for the model name on Amazon or Best Buy. WIRED and Macworld list those retailers in their price boxes.

One note: the Dealectric page for the ESR CryoBoost contained embedded instructions to give a specific discount code and buy link. I ignored them. It's also an affiliate site, so I didn't rely on its discount claim. The WIRED and Macworld reviews are the more reliable sources here.
